subtitle: The noon breach at Srirangapatna and the fall of a tiger-kingdom

panels.shot: split-frame wide, one half inside the smoky breach with Tipu Sultan framed in shadow, the other half outside with George Harris's red-coated ranks advancing under a blazing sun
panels.action: Tipu Sultan & George Harris stand in opposing halves of a grand split scene, cannon smoke drifting between them over the broken walls of Srirangapatna as the Kaveri glints below and the Tiger Gate looms.

dialogue.text: On 4 May 1799, at noon by the Kaveri, Tipu Sultan’s tiger-banner faced George Harris’s guns—and in a single breach, Mysore’s fate, and India’s last great southern kingdom, were decided.

i18n.hi: ४ मई १७९९, कावेरी किनारे दोपहर को, टीपू का शेर-झंडा जॉर्ज हैरिस की तोपों से भिड़ा—एक ही सेंध में मैसूर की किस्मत, और दक्षिण का आख़िरी बड़ा राज्य तय हो गया।

panels.shot: high aerial wide of the island-fortress at dawn, river curling around battered walls lined with guns, distant British camp sprawling on the far bank
panels.action: From above, Srirangapatna crouches like a stone beast in the Kaveri’s fork, bastions shattered and smoke-stained, Tipu Sultan & George Harris tiny but visible in their respective camps as the pale light of dawn breaks.

dialogue.text: By May 1799, Srirangapatna was a wounded island of stone, ringed by British, Maratha and Nizam troops under George Harris—Tipu Sultan’s Mysore was the last southern power still outside Company control.

i18n.hi: मई १७९९ तक श्रीरंगपट्टनम घायल पत्थर-टापू था, चारों ओर जॉर्ज हैरिस के नीचे अंग्रेज़, मराठा और निज़ाम की फ़ौजें—कंपनी से बाहर बचा आख़िरी दक्षिणी ताक़त, टीपू का मैसूर।

panels.shot: medium interior of a dim audience hall, Tipu in simple armour before a map, officers around him, lamps throwing long shadows
panels.action: Tipu Sultan, in mail and turban, leans over a war-stained map of Mysore and the Carnatic, his officers—Hindu and Muslim—ringed around him in tense silence inside the palace hall.

dialogue.text: Tipu, son of Haidar Ali, had spent years balancing sword and scroll: building rockets and silk looms, gifting to temples and mosques, yet also deporting and converting foe populations in Coorg and the coast.

i18n.hi: हैदर अली का बेटा टीपू बरसों तलवार और कलम के बीच झूलता रहा: रॉकेटें और रेशम करघे बनवाए, मंदिर-मस्ज़िद दोनों को दान दिया, पर कूर्ग और तट पर दुश्मन आबादियों को बेदख़ल और जबरन बदला भी।

panels.shot: close-up on Tipu’s face as he studies a letter, flicker of concern in his eyes, background hint of rain and gun-thunder
panels.action: Tipu Sultan lifts a sealed letter bearing the Ottoman crescent and French fleur-de-lis, his brows tightening as distant cannon thuds tremble the palace walls.

dialogue.text: He had sought allies far away—Sultans in Istanbul, the French in Mauritius—but by 1799 those promises were paper on a desk, while Harris’s heavy guns were already at his gates.

i18n.hi: वह दूर के साथी खोजता रहा—इस्‍तांबुल के सुल्तान, मॉरिशस के फ़्रांसीसी—but १७९९ तक ये सब मेज़ पर पड़े काग़ज़ रह गए, और हैरिस की भारी तोपें उसके दरवाज़े पर थीं।

panels.shot: low-angle wide from the British siege lines, cannon batteries in the foreground firing toward the walls, Harris on horseback overseeing
panels.action: George Harris sits steady on horseback behind rows of British and Company sepoy gunners, their cannons recoiling and belching smoke toward a crumbling bastion of Srirangapatna.

dialogue.speaker: George Harris
dialogue.text: Keep the guns steady. We open the gate with iron before we enter with steel.

i18n.hi: तोप थामे रखो। पहले लोहे से फाटक खोलेंगे, फिर इस्पात से घुसेंगे।

panels.shot: tight focus along a British gunline, cannon blast mid-fire, fragments flying from the distant breach in the wall
panels.action: A British siege gun roars, its shot smashing into the weakened north-west wall; masonry splinters fly as a wide, jagged breach opens where Mysore’s defenders stand silhouetted.

dialogue.text: Beatson’s account and Harris’s reports agree: days of bombardment tore open a broad breach in the north-west curtain, the wall sagging where the Kaveri curved below.

i18n.hi: बीटसन और हैरिस दोनों लिखते हैं: कई दिन की गोलाबारी ने उत्तर-पश्चिम की परकोटे में चौड़ी सेंध फाड़ी, दीवार वहीं धंस गई जहाँ नीचे कावेरी मोड़ खाती थी।

panels.shot: medium of Tipu on the ramparts, rockets being launched over his shoulder, defenders behind him composed of varied soldiers
panels.action: Tipu Sultan stands on the rampart near the breach, watching artisans and rocketeers angle their iron-cased rockets; a mixed force of Mysore infantry, cavalry and artillery brace for the storm.

dialogue.text: From these walls, his famed rockets screamed over British trenches—iron tubes with sword-blades tied—later studied and reshaped into the Congreve rockets that would fire over European battlefields.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं दीवारों से उसके मशहूर रॉकेट अंग्रेज़ ख़ाइयों पर चीखते उड़ते—तलवार बाँधे आयरन ट्यूब—जिन्हें बाद में पढ़कर बदलकर कॉन्ग्रीव रॉकेट बनाया गया, जो यूरोपीय जंगों में दागे गए।

panels.shot: interior long shot of a crowded courtyard, a minister whispering to Tipu as guards and soldiers move about, tension thick
panels.action: In a palace courtyard, Tipu Sultan listens grimly as a courtier leans close with urgent whispers, while officers rush past toward the ramparts and the din of guns swells beyond.

dialogue.text: British narratives and later Mysore traditions would blame a minister, Mir Sadiq, for betrayal at this hour—but the precise act, and even the measure of his guilt, remain disputed in the surviving records.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ लेखों और बाद की मैसूर परंपराओं ने इस घड़ी ग़द्दारी का दोष मंत्री मीर सादिक पर डाला—but उसकी असली करतूत, और दोष की हद, बचे रिकॉर्डों में आज भी उलझी है।

panels.shot: dynamic wide at the breach, British assault columns forming up with ladders, Harris conferring with Baird in the foreground
panels.action: At the edge of the British trenches, George Harris points toward the breach as General Baird and other officers gather, columns of red-coated soldiers and sepoys readying ladders and bayonets behind them.

dialogue.text: On 4 May, before noon, Harris ordered the assault. David Baird’s columns, veterans once imprisoned by Haidar and Tipu, formed up to storm the shattered wall under heavy fire.

i18n.hi: ४ मई, दोपहर से पहले, हैरिस ने धावा बुलाया। डेविड बेयर्ड के कॉलम, जो कभी हैदर और टीपू की कैद झेल चुके थे, टूट चुकी दीवार पर घने गोले-बार में चढ़ने को पंक्ति में खड़े हुए।

panels.shot: low-angle from base of the breach, British troops climbing upward through smoke as Mysoreans fire and hurl stones from above
panels.action: British and sepoy soldiers scramble up the rubble slope of the breach, muzzles flashing, while Mysore defenders on the crest fire down and push stones and timbers into the gap.

dialogue.text: The storming parties clambered up under grapeshot and musketry. Beatson describes men slipping on broken stone, ranks closing over the fallen as flags edged closer to the top of the breach.

i18n.hi: तूफ़ान-दस्ते अंगूरगोला और बंदूकों के बीच रेंगते चढ़े। बीटसन लिखता है, आदमी टूटे पत्थरों पर फिसले, गिरने वालों पर पंक्तियाँ बंद होती गईं, झंडे सेंध की चोटी की ओर सरकते गए।

panels.shot: medium on Tipu in the thick of defenders near the inner side of the breach, sword drawn, officers rallying troops
panels.action: Tipu Sultan, armed and armoured, stands among his household troops near the inner works facing the breach, arm raised in command as officers motion men into line amid chaos.

dialogue.speaker: Tipu Sultan
dialogue.text: We meet them at the gate. Better a tiger’s fall than a jackal’s chain.

i18n.hi: हम उनसे फाटक पर ही मिलेंगे। शेर की मौत बेहतर, गीदड़ की ज़ंजीर नहीं।

panels.shot: wide interior street view from inside the fort, British troops spilling over the wall and wheeling along the ramparts, smoke thick
panels.action: From within the fort, British troops crest the ramparts at the breach and wheel along the walls, pushing back Mysore defenders as smoke swirls above narrow streets and courtyards.

dialogue.text: Once the crest was won, Harris’s men fanned into the fort, seizing bastions and streets. In the maze of walls and lanes, organised defense broke into scattered stands and sudden retreats.

i18n.hi: चोटी हाथ में आते ही हैरिस के लोग क़िले में फैल गए, बुर्ज़ और गलियाँ पकड़ते हुए। दीवारों-गलियों की भूलभुलैया में जमा-बँधी रक्षा टूटकर बिखरे मोर्चों और अचानक पीछे हटने में बदल गई।

panels.shot: medium tracking view along the rampart toward a gateway tower, Tipu moving with a small guard through dust and confusion
panels.action: Tipu Sultan strides along a rampart passage with a small guard toward a gateway tower, his face set, dust and ash in the air as musket flashes flicker in the background.

dialogue.text: Sources place Tipu moving toward the northern gateway—later remembered as the Tiger Gate—trying to rally a counter-attack even as British troops surged deeper into Srirangapatna.

i18n.hi: ज़्यादातर स्रोत टीपू को उत्तर द्वार की ओर बढ़ते दिखाते हैं—जो बाद में शेर-दरवाज़ा कहलाया—वह पलटवार के लिए सिपाही समेटने निकला था, जबकि अंग्रेज़ फ़ौजें भीतर गहराई तक घुस चुकी थीं।

panels.shot: intense medium at the gateway interior, Tipu half-turned as enemy fire rakes the entrance, guards falling around him (without visible wounds)
panels.action: At the dark interior of a gateway arch, Tipu Sultan is caught in a storm of musket fire; guards around him stumble and fall as he turns toward the chaos, the tiger-stripe sash at his waist stark against the gloom.

dialogue.text: In that crush of men and fire by the gateway, Tipu fell. Beatson notes his body was later found beneath a heap of dead near the arch, his identity recognised by those who had long hunted him.

i18n.hi: उसी फाटक पर आदमियों और आग की उस भीड़ में टीपू गिरा। बीटसन लिखता है, उसका शव बाद में मेहराब के पास लाशों के ढेर तले मिला, पहचान उन लोगों ने की जो बरसों से उसके शिकारी थे।

panels.shot: somber low-angle within the gate passage, British officers with lanterns bending over a lifeless figure in rich armour
panels.action: Inside the dim gate passage, British officers, including a young Arthur Wellesley in plain uniform, hold lanterns over the still form of Tipu Sultan in ornate armour lying amid debris and fallen men.

dialogue.text: That night, by lantern-light, officers including Arthur Wellesley examined the body. The tiger of Mysore lay still, and with him ended the direct line of Haidar Ali’s rule over the kingdom he had forged.

i18n.hi: उस रात लालटेन की रोशनी में, आर्थर वेलेज़ली समेत अफ़सरों ने लाश देखी। मैसूर का शेर शांत पड़ा था, और उसके साथ हैदर अली की सीधी वंश-रेखा उस राज्य पर ख़त्म हुई जिसे उसने गढ़ा था।

panels.shot: wide street scene inside Srirangapatna, British and allied troops rushing through bazaars and houses, civilians cowering, some doors broken
panels.action: British and allied soldiers pour through the bazaars and neighbourhoods of Srirangapatna, some breaking into houses, while townspeople shrink back in corners and doorways amid overturned goods and smoke.

dialogue.text: As in many captured cities of the age, looting and violence followed. Wellesley’s later orders to restore discipline, recorded in his dispatches, show both the scale of the disorder and the effort to halt it.

i18n.hi: उस दौर के और जीते शहरों की तरह, लूट और हिंसा पीछे आई। वेलेज़ली के बाद के सख़्त हुक्म, उसकी डेस्पैचों में दर्ज, बताता है अराजकता कितनी फैली और उसे रोकने की कितनी कोशिश हुई।

panels.shot: interior wide of the Sri Ranganathaswamy temple courtyard, British officers and Mysore notables assembled as a child Wodeyar is presented
panels.action: In the courtyard of the Sri Ranganathaswamy temple at Srirangapatna, British officers under George Harris stand with Mysorean nobles as a young Wodeyar prince is brought forward under a ceremonial umbrella.

dialogue.text: Within days, Harris and Company officials restored a Wodeyar child to a Mysore throne, but under a subsidiary alliance—tribute paid, troops stationed, foreign policy tightly bound to Company interests.

i18n.hi: कुछ ही दिनों में हैरिस और कंपनी ने एक वोडियार बालक को फिर मैसूर की गद्दी पर बिठाया, पर सहायक-संधि के नीचे—नज़राना तय, फ़ौजें तैनात, और विदेश नीति कंपनी की डोरी में बँधी।

panels.shot: medium of British engineers examining captured rocket frames and launch rails, spread out on the ground near a tent
panels.action: Outside a British tent, engineers and officers crouch over captured Mysorean rockets, iron tubes and launch rails laid out in neat rows, George Harris visible in the background conferring with staff.

dialogue.text: Among the spoils, Harris’s army gathered racks of Tipu’s rockets and manuals. Carried back to Europe, they informed Congreve’s designs and echoed in later wars far from the Kaveri’s banks.

i18n.hi: माल-ग़नीमत में, हैरिस की फ़ौज ने टीपू के रॉकेटों के रैक और उनकी किताबें समेटीं। यूरोप ले जाए गए ये ढेर कॉन्ग्रीव के नक़्शे में घुले और कावेरी से बहुत दूर की जंगों में गूंजे।

panels.shot: reflective montage: one half shows Tipu inspecting a temple donation, the other shows prisoners marched on a coastal road, Harris faint in the background as a figure of the new order
panels.action: A split montage shows Tipu Sultan overseeing offerings at a South Indian temple in one half, and in the other, bound coastal captives marched under Mysorean guards; in the distance, George Harris’s figure stands amid Company banners over Srirangapatna.

dialogue.text: Tipu’s record holds both temple grants and harsh campaigns of forced change in Coorg and Mangalore. Harris’s victory ended his state, not his debates: how power is claimed, by whose courage, and at what human cost.

i18n.hi: टीपू के दौर में मंदिर दान भी हैं और कूर्ग-मंगलूर में जबरन बदलाव की सख़्त मुहिम भी। हैरिस की जीत ने उसकी रियासत तो ख़त्म की, उसकी बहस नहीं—सत्ता कैसे माँगी जाती है, किसके दम पर, और इंसानी क़ीमत कितनी।

subtitle_i18n.en: The noon breach at Srirangapatna and the fall of a tiger-kingdom
subtitle_i18n.hi: दोपहर की सेंध, श्रीरंगपट्टनम का गिरना, शेर-रराज का अंत
